clue.text: German order for cab

parts.note: Hans is a typical German man's name
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A German customer barks instructions at a taxi driver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' looks like a command but is an honour: OM, the Order of Merit.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage for hire, the Victorian forerunner of the taxi.

clue.text: An inability to kick?

parts.note: to kick a habit is to give it up, so a dependency is being unable to

explanation.walkthrough: 'kick' suggests football, but 'kick the habit' means quit.
explanation.definitionFit: Dependency on a drug or habit is exactly being unable to give it up.

clue.text: Having injected a drug, grew fast

definitions.meaning: slang for having taken a drug by needle
to grow quickly, as a teenager does

explanation.surface: A teenager who took drugs had a growth spurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are phrasal verbs: injecting heroin and sprouting suddenly in height.

clue.text: Young adult going short for a very long time

indicators.note: going short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a millennial is a young adult of the generation born around 1980-2000

explanation.surface: A young person goes without for a long period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Thousands of years make an extremely long span, used loosely for ages.

clue.text: Hate to sack someone from the English cricket team?

definitions.text: to sack someone from the English cricket team?
definitions.meaning: to remove a player from the England Test side, the top international form of cricket

explanation.surface: Someone loathes the idea of dropping a player from the England side.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is an international cricket match; 'de-' undoes, so to de-test a player is a joke coinage for dropping them.
explanation.definitionFit: Loathing something intensely is a straightforward synonym of hating it.

clue.text: Amount owed: one less makes no difference

definitions.text: Amount owed: one less makes no difference

parts.words: Amount owed: one less makes no difference
parts.note: remove I (one) from the word and you still have a sum owing, so losing one changes nothing

explanation.walkthrough: Taking the I (one) out of DEBIT leaves DEBT, which still means an amount owed.
explanation.definitionFit: An entry recording money due in an account is a sum owing.

clue.text: Picking up pet, I become reticent

indicators.note: in a down clue picking up lifts the word, so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a cat is a typical pet
to turn is to become, as milk turns sour

explanation.surface: Someone becomes withdrawn while lifting a pet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picking up' turns CAT into TAC, read upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Being reserved and uncommunicative, saying little, is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Crack very visible in bottom of shoe

indicators.note: visible in means the letter can be seen sitting within the word

parts.note: the sole is the underside of a shoe

explanation.surface: A crack can be seen in the bottom of a shoe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' looks like a split in leather but means work out, as a code.
explanation.definitionFit: To crack a puzzle or code is to work out its answer.

clue.text: Sleeping bag for curling up?

definitions.meaning: bedding carried by campers and rolled up when not in use
a playful reading: something to roll into when going to bed

explanation.surface: A camper chooses a sleeping bag to curl up in.
explanation.definitionFit: Rolled bedding used by campers and soldiers is a close equivalent of a sleeping bag.

clue.text: First-day cover?

parts.note: a first-day cover is a stamp-collecting item, but here it is a covering for a newborn on day one

explanation.walkthrough: A first-day cover is an envelope with a new stamp postmarked on its day of issue; here it is read as a wrap for an infant.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft wrap for a newborn infant is the first thing to cover it.

clue.text: Rural infection almost a severe pain

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: a bug is an informal word for an infection
colic is a severe abdominal pain

explanation.surface: A country illness that is nearly agonising.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastoral and countryside matters are described with this literary adjective.

clue.text: Dejected as ridge collapsed

parts.note: a crest is the ridge or top of a hill
fallen means having collapsed

explanation.surface: Someone feels down as the ridge gave way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird lowering its crest pictures disappointment, hence downcast.

clue.text: Why climb Everest? Ice sheet's a brute to struggle with

indicators.note: struggle suggests the letters writhing about into a new order

explanation.surface: A climber explains why Everest is tough: its ice sheet is brutal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to struggle with' rearranges the letters of ICE SHEETS A BRUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: George Mallory's famous reply when asked his motive for attempting the world's highest mountain.

clue.text: Radar image showing temporary deviation

definitions.meaning: a small spot of light on a radar screen
a brief, unimportant dip or departure from a trend

explanation.surface: A radar screen shows a brief anomaly.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are a small momentary flicker, on a screen or in a trend.

clue.text: Their thing turned out to be justified

indicators.note: turned out suggests the letters being turned over into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Their pet project proved to be vindicated in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out' rearranges THEIR THING; 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being correct or having justice on your side is an idiom for being justified.

clue.text: Fail to complete coronation ceremony, needing old piece of silver

parts.note: doing only half of something is failing to finish it
to crown is the act performed at a coronation

explanation.surface: A botched coronation needs a silver coin.
explanation.walkthrough: The half crown was a pre-decimal British coin worth two shillings and sixpence; 'needing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This pre-1971 British coin was originally minted in silver.

clue.text: Lame displays of light entertainment

parts.note: a game leg is a lame one
shows means displays

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses lightweight TV as feeble displays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lame' seems to mean feeble but gives GAME, an old word for lame, as in a game leg.
explanation.definitionFit: Quiz programmes with contestants and prizes are a staple of light TV entertainment.

clue.text: Importance of sex in monastery

indicators.note: in puts the slang word inside the religious house

parts.note: a priory is a monastery run by a prior
it is a coy slang word for sex

explanation.surface: A scandalous question about how much sex matters in a monastery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Precedence or first place in order of urgency is what this word means.

clue.text: Unusually, mob ran off — mate followed

indicators.note: followed puts the partner after the scrambled letters
off suggests the letters gone wrong and so rearranged

parts.note: an ally is a friend or mate

explanation.surface: Strangely, a crowd ran away and then a friend went after them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' looks like an anagram signal but is the definition; 'off' is the real one, rearranging MOB RAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in an atypical, out-of-the-ordinary way is a synonym.

clue.text: Some item: man and woman

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A couple, man and woman, described as an item.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'and woman' included the link word 'and', which cannot stand in for a name; the definition is just 'woman'.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name, as in Jane Austen's heroine, stands for a woman.

clue.text: Raided by the police and broken

explanation.surface: A place was raided by the police and wrecked.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal senses: nicked by the police, and smashed or broken.

clue.text: Retain barrister, but refuse to speak

definitions.meaning: to keep one's own counsel, a lawyer, on retainer
to keep quiet about one's thoughts

explanation.surface: A defendant hires a lawyer but stays silent.
explanation.walkthrough: Counsel is a barrister, a courtroom lawyer in Britain, so the phrase read literally means hanging on to your lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for keeping your opinions and plans private and saying nothing.

clue.text: How teeth are said to appear to explode

definitions.text: How teeth are said to appear
definitions.meaning: dentists speak of new teeth breaking through the gum this way
to burst out violently, as a volcano does

explanation.surface: A dentist's question about how teeth come through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A volcano bursting violently and a tooth breaking through gum share one verb.

clue.text: This on top of face is embarrassing? Offer encouragement!

definitions.text: This on top of face is embarrassing?
definitions.meaning: having ... your face means being embarrassed

explanation.surface: An awkward moment followed by a cheer to carry on.
explanation.definitionFit: To urge or goad someone into action is to spur them forward.

clue.text: Try to sell time travel

definitions.note: a verb phrase; the answer is its -ing form, trying to sell

parts.note: an outing is a trip, a bit of travel

explanation.surface: A salesman pitches a time-travel package.
explanation.definitionFit: Hawking wares aggressively in public is a form of trying to make a sale.

clue.text: A couple in our navy are obsolete

indicators.note: in puts the pair inside the word our

parts.note: a couple is two

explanation.surface: Some old ships in our fleet are past it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' does the inserting; 'our' is used as written, not as a possessive, and 'are' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worn out by use is no longer serviceable, so out of date.

clue.text: Remain a while, having nothing nasty to deal with

indicators.note: dealing cards shuffles and hands them out, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: O, the zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: Someone stays on a little longer since there is nothing unpleasant to face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to deal with' rearranges O and NASTY; 'having' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To linger or continue somewhere beyond the expected time is a phrasal verb of staying.

clue.text: One unsuited as a colonist

parts.note: unsuited means wearing no suit, and the colony is a naturist colony

explanation.walkthrough: 'unsuited' suggests unfit for colonising, but means unclothed; a colonist is a member of a nudist colony.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturist, someone going without clothes, would be unclothed in such a colony.
